## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Tacasārajātaka* (Ja 368) is a birth story in the Pali *Jātaka* collection [SuttaCentral]. Set at Jetavana, the discourse was delivered by the Buddha concerning the Perfection of Wisdom (*paññāpāramī*), observing that the Tathāgata was similarly wise and resourceful in past lives [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1883]. The narrative recalls an ancient time when Brahmadatta was reigning in Bārāṇasī, opening with the verse beginning *Amittahatthatthagatā ti* [Fausböll 1883]. In the concluding identification (*samodhāna*), the Buddha reveals that the King of Bārāṇasī was Ānanda, the other youths were senior theras (*therānutherā*), and the wise youth (*paṇḍitadārako*) was the Buddha himself in a former birth [Fausböll 1883].
SuttaCentral notes passage-level parallels between the *Tacasārajātaka* and two suttas from the *Pañcakanipāta* of the *Aṅguttara Nikāya*: the *Alabbhanīyaṭhānasutta* (AN 5.48) and the *Nāradasutta* (AN 5.50) [SuttaCentral]. Computational analysis via DharmaNexus confirms this relationship, registering four shared passages (1,004 characters) with the *Pañcakanipāta* (PA_an_5), with a major alignment linking Ja 368 §2.1–5.4 to AN 5.48 §48.7.1–48.10.4 at 0.98 similarity [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also records three matches (798 characters) with the commentary in the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (Tatiyo bhāgo) [DharmaNexus].
